subject: SOC 2 / SIG follow-up: rolling scan window, emergency hotfix SLA and CVE ownership
messages:
From: BrightAudit (auditor) <auditor@brightaudit.com>
To: lauren_bishop@redwood.com
Cc: security@penumbra.io
Date: 2028-05-01T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: SOC 2 SIG follow-up: scan cadence evidence + hotfix SLA clarification

Hi Lauren,

Following our SIG review last week we need a short packet confirming Redwood's vulnerability management cadence and concrete SLAs for emergency CVE remediation (Critical / High). Specifically the auditor wants:

- The rolling-scan window (how often assets are scanned, how rolling windows are defined across groups)
- Measured SLA for Critical CVE hotfixes (we've seen '48-72 hours' in slides; need an explicit attestation)
- Escalation and ownership path for externally-reported CVEs (who is the PoC, how does the triage happen)
- Evidence: scan schedule, sample scan logs, and an attestation signed by an owner for SOC 2 binder

Can you provide a one-page attestation and an export of the scan cadence/schedule? Auditor would like to close this item by next Tuesday. Penumbra is on the thread for any technical follow-ups.

Thanks,
Erin McCall
Senior Auditor, BrightAudit

---
Note: this is a request for evidence only. If you have an internal packet or playbook we can link to that as well (DocuSign or Drive link acceptable).

From: lauren_bishop <lauren_bishop@redwood.com>
To: BrightAudit (auditor) <auditor@brightaudit.com>
Cc: Penumbra Security <security@penumbra.io>, marissa_cole@redwood.com
Date: 2028-05-01T11:05:00-07:00
Subject: Re: SOC 2 SIG follow-up: scan cadence evidence + hotfix SLA clarification

Hi Erin — thanks for the clear ask. Short answers up front and attachments below.

1) Rolling-scan window:
   - All production VPCs are on a rolling vulnerability scan schedule that completes a full asset sweep every 7 days.
   - Hosts are grouped by service domain; groups are staggered so each group runs a fresh full-scan once per week while critical surface scans run nightly (targeted checks for package vulns and OSS CVEs).

2) Hotfix SLA (attested):
   - Critical CVEs: mitigation plan acknowledged within 4 hours; remediation/patch applied OR mitigated within 48 hours of confirmation on triage.
   - High CVEs: remediation applied or compensated within 7 days.
   - Exceptions: documented and approved by Security & Engineering with compensating controls if timelines cannot be met.

3) Escalation / ownership:
   - External reports: security@redwood.com intake -> Security Triage -> assign to oncall service owner (engineering lead).
   - Owner responsibilities: validate, categorize severity, open remediation ticket, and update stakeholders.

Attachments included: scan schedule CSV and a draft attestation PDF (vm-attestation-20280505.pdf). Also attached a short hotfix playbook (cve-hotfix-playbook.md). The attestation is signed by our security lead and formatted for inclusion in your SOC 2 binder.

I'll loop in Marissa to confirm the scan export and provide sample logs for the week of 2028-04-24 as evidence. If you'd like a DocuSign-signed copy let me know and we'll route it.

Best,
Lauren Bishop
Head of Trust & Controls
Redwood Inference

Attachment stubs: redwood_scan_schedule_rolling_windows.csv (CSV export, 3 columns: group, schedule_day, nightly_target_checks), vm-attestation-20280505.pdf (signed), cve-hotfix-playbook.md

From: marissa_cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>

Lauren — quick internal confirmation before we publish the packet to BrightAudit / Penumbra.

- The CSV export is attached (redwood_scan_schedule_rolling_windows.csv). It enumerates group windows and shows automated staggered scans.
- Sample logs: I pulled nightly targeted scan outputs for 2028-04-24 to 2028-04-30 and redacted IPs for distribution; these are in the shared Drive link in our response.
- On SLAs: Operations and oncall confirm Critical 48-hour remediation commitment is operational for fully-supported services. For third-party hosted components we document exceptions and escalate to product security — we have a queue for mitigation tasks.

Action items for us:

2) If BrightAudit needs DocuSign, I'll prep the envelope and route to Lauren for sign-off.
3) Kimberley / Ops — please approve the exception language for legacy third-party components.

Thanks — ping me if you want the redacted logs attached to the thread or only via Drive.

Marissa Cole

Redwood Inference

Thanks,
